content: Community Health Workers (CHWs) are individuals who are deeply trusted by the communities they serve. They act as a vital link between healthcare systems and populations that are often underserved or marginalized. Their responsibilities include conducting outreach efforts to engage community members, advocating for the needs and rights of individuals within the community, and providing essential social support to those in need. They also assist in connecting individuals to appropriate healthcare services by making referrals. In certain situations, CHWs may carry out specific clinical tasks, but only under the direct supervision of licensed healthcare professionals.
